date_note: Cyber Kendra's page is dated Nov 20 but states the situation as of Nov 19; published date taken as Nov 19.
title: FastUnlock: unpatched Windows 11 Narrator flaw lets an attacker with physical access bypass the lock screen and BitLocker, researcher claims
summary: A researcher using the names Chaotic Eclipse and Nightmare-Eclipse posted 'FastUnlock' on GitHub without coordinating with Microsoft. Cyber Kendra says the researcher claims a Narrator lock-screen flaw lets someone with physical access bypass BitLocker on Windows 11 26H2 in about five minutes; it needs an account linked to a Microsoft account. The Hacker News says ThreatLocker ran a program from the lock screen but the method does not break encryption. No CVE or Microsoft fix.
plain: A researcher says a lost or stolen Windows 11 laptop could be unlocked using the screen reader feature. Microsoft has published no fix or advisory yet.
exec: Matters for lost or stolen laptops that rely on BitLocker; physical access is required and no attacks in the wild are reported.
action: Until Microsoft responds, consider blocking Narrator on the lock screen with AppLocker or a restrictive DACL (the researcher's suggestion; test first) and keep devices physically secured.

key_findings: No CVE as of Nov 19; no Microsoft advisory, fix or workaround listed.
Needs physical access and a local account linked to a Microsoft account.
Researcher suggests blocking Narrator via AppLocker or a custom DACL as a possible fix.
recommendations: Secure devices physically; consider blocking Narrator until a patch ships.

validation.note: Cyber Kendra and Security Affairs report the researcher's release and claims. The Hacker News (Nov 20) reports ThreatLocker tested it and said it works, running a program from the lock screen under a limited non-administrator account; it says it does not break BitLocker encryption. Microsoft has published no confirmation, CVE or fix; no in-the-wild use reported. Still a claim.
